land.text: the steppe of the Eastern Turkic Khaganate, entered by the Xueyantuo leader in 627

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Eastern Göktürks row ends 632; the Tang conquered the Eastern Turks in 630.

successors.note: 'In 646 the Tang dynasty conquered the Xueyantuo.' Thirteen Tiele and Uyghur tribes surrendered on 9 January 647.

land.text: the Uyghur tribes, who helped defeat the Xueyantuo in 646 and later founded the Uyghur Khaganate

successors.note: Held by the Tang protectorate 647-682, then by the Second Turkic Khaganate.

capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Otuken'; the page also says the Xueyantuo settled in the Tola valley in northern Mongolia after 627.

rulers.name: Zhenzhu Khan (Yinan-erkin)
rulers.note: The infobox list gives 628-645; the page dates the declaration to 629.

correction.text: Otuken and the Tola valley in northern Mongolia

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row (Cliopatria's Eastern Göktürks row ends 632 and the Tang row then draws the plateau from 633). The page gives no area. 'The Xueyantuo's vast khaganate spanned from the Altai Mountains to the Gobi Desert'; they 'settled in the Tola valley in northern Mongolia after 627'; capital Otuken. Only the Tola valley and Otuken are drawn for 629: the khaganate spans the whole of northern Mongolia only after the Eastern Turks fall in March 630 (next keyframe, where northern Mongolia without the Gobi is the reading; the South Gobi and Inner Mongolia stay Tang or Turkic).

correction.text: the khaganate 'from the Altai Mountains to the Gobi Desert': northern Mongolia

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. After the Tang and the Xueyantuo beat the Eastern Turks on 27 March 630, the khaganate spans 'from the Altai Mountains to the Gobi Desert' (Xueyantuo page).

union.text: the land 'between the Yellow River and Gobi' north of the Ordos Loop, from which the Xueyantuo drove the Ashina Turks

correction.text: northern Mongolia without the Gobi, with the Hetao plain north of the Ordos Loop

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the 630 shape plus the Hetao plain outside the Ordos. 'Taizong made them live between the Yellow River and Gobi under Qilibi Khan (639-643)'; 'In 642 the Xueyantuo drove them south of the river' (Eastern Turkic Khaganate page; 'them' are the Ashina, the river the Yellow River; the page does not name Hetao). The Hetao plain is the researcher's reading of 'between the Yellow River and Gobi', as in the eastern-gokturks dossier (ledger 12, 642 loss, confidence 2); the Ordos Loop stays with the Ashina. The Xueyantuo page opened has nothing dated 641, 642 or 643. The page gives no area.

region.text: Otuken and the Tola valley in northern Mongolia

ledger.note: 629: Yinan-erkin declares himself khagan of the Xueyantuo. 'In 629 the Xueyantuo Yinan-erkin declared himself' khagan; the infobox says 'Established 628' and the revolt of 627 had them entering the Eastern Turkic Khaganate's territory; 'The Tang recognized the khaganate quickly, as a counterweight to the Eastern Turks.'

region.text: the khaganate 'from the Altai Mountains to the Gobi Desert': northern Mongolia

ledger.note: 27 March 630: the Xueyantuo and the Tang crush the Eastern Turks in the Yin Mountains. 'On March 27, 630, the Xueyantuo allied with the Tang to defeat the Eastern Turkic Khaganate in the Yin Mountains' (Xueyantuo page); the Eastern Turkic page has the Tang conquest in 630 and the Turks settled between the Yellow River and the Gobi, so the Xueyantuo take the plateau north of the Gobi.

region.text: the land 'between the Yellow River and Gobi' north of the Ordos Loop, from which the Xueyantuo drove the Ashina Turks

ledger.note: 642: the Xueyantuo drive the Ashina Turks south of the Yellow River. 'In 642 the Xueyantuo drove them south of the river' (Eastern Turkic Khaganate page), after the Tang had settled the Turks 'between the Yellow River and Gobi under Qilibi Khan (639-643)'. The year is the page's; the land (Hetao outside the Ordos) is the researcher's reading, matching the eastern-gokturks dossier's 642 loss.

region.text: the khaganate 'from the Altai Mountains to the Gobi Desert': northern Mongolia

ledger.note: 1 August 646: the Tang and the Uyghurs destroy the Xueyantuo. 'On August 1, 646, the Xueyantuo were defeated by the Uyghurs and the Tang'; 'The Xueyantuo's Duomi Khan was killed by the Uyghurs'; the remnants were destroyed 'two years later, on September 15'; the Pacify the North page: 'In 646 the Tang dynasty conquered the Xueyantuo'.

wars.name: Xueyantuo revolt against the Eastern Turks

zones.text: the khaganate 'from the Altai Mountains to the Gobi Desert': northern Mongolia

wars.outcome: In 627 the Xueyantuo entered the Eastern Turkic Khaganate; the Uyghur leader split from the confederation after the victory; on 27 March 630 the Xueyantuo and the Tang beat the Eastern Turks in the Yin Mountains.

wars.name: Xueyantuo drive the Ashina Turks south of the Yellow River

zones.text: the land 'between the Yellow River and Gobi' north of the Ordos Loop, from which the Xueyantuo drove the Ashina Turks

wars.outcome: 'In 642 the Xueyantuo drove them south of the river': the Ashina Turks, settled by Taizong between the Yellow River and the Gobi from 639, lose the Hetao plain.
wars.note: The eastern-gokturks dossier adds, from the Ashina Simo page, an attack in winter 641; not re-read here.

wars.name: Tang-Uyghur conquest of the Xueyantuo

zones.text: the khaganate 'from the Altai Mountains to the Gobi Desert': northern Mongolia

wars.outcome: On 1 August 646 the Tang general Li Daozong, with the Uyghurs, crushed the Xueyantuo; Duomi Khan was killed by the Uyghurs; thirteen Tiele and Uyghur tribes surrendered on 9 January 647 and the Yanran Protectorate was created on 10 April.
wars.note: The Xueyantuo page gives the final destruction of the remnants 'two years later'.

certainty.note: A tribal confederation of the steppe: the page gives mountains and a desert as edges.

notes: New state (Cliopatria lacks the Xueyantuo; the Tang dossier example names them as a counterpart 629-646). The infobox gives 628 and a disestablishment of '723 (?-723 under Second Turkic Khaganate)'; the text dates the formal declaration to 629 and the defeat to 646, which the dossier uses. The Tang example (ea-04) draws the plateau as direct Tang land 633-681 in Cliopatria; this dossier draws it as Xueyantuo until 646 and the Yanran Protectorate takes it from 647 (Tang dossier). Revised after review (ia-01-x fix pass): the Eastern Turkic Khaganate page (cited here) does date a 642 campaign, 'In 642 the Xueyantuo drove them south of the river', so the dossier now has a 642 gain of Hetao outside the Ordos from eastern-gokturks (ledger 2, keyframe xueyantuo_642, a war), mirroring eastern-gokturks ledger 12; the land is the researcher's reading of 'between the Yellow River and Gobi', the page names no region. The Xueyantuo page itself has nothing dated 641, 642 or 643, and neither page opened mentions the Battle of Mount Ma'i; the war with the Tang is dated only 646. Rulers are the three khans of the Xueyantuo page's list (Zhenzhu 628-645, Duomi 645-646, Yitewushi 646); the dossier starts Zhenzhu in 629, the page's declaration year. Gazetteer names used (Outer Mongolia, Gobi, Orkhon Valley, Ulaanbaatar) resolve.
